content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To remove health hazards from your backyard, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Purchase heavy-duty puncture-proof disposal bags (30 minutes)
Step 2. Rent a professional wood chipper for fallen debris (2 hours)
Step 3. Apply eco-friendly neutralizer to acidic soil patches (45 minutes)
Step 4. Bag and seal asbestos-laden insulation found in the shed (3 hours)
Step 5. Research local regulations for hazardous waste disposal (1 hour)
Step 6. Final inspection of the perimeter for remaining risks (1 hour)
Step 7. Scrub the concrete patio to remove toxic algae (2 hours)
Step 8. Schedule a pickup for chemical waste containers (15 minutes)
Step 9. Replace old, lead-painted fence pickets (6 hours)
Step 10. Identify outdated pesticides stored in the garage (20 minutes)
Step 11. Label all biohazard bags for the disposal team (40 minutes)
Step 12. Dismantle the rusted, unstable swing set (4 hours)
Step 13. Inventory all structural hazards in the yard (1 hour)
Step 14. Mix a biodegradable cleaning solution (10 minutes)
Step 15. Locate underground utility lines before digging (3 hours)
Step 16. Inspect the old shed for structural integrity and lead (2 hours)
Step 17. Treat the standing water for mosquito larvae (30 minutes)
Step 18. Don full-body protective gear and respirators (20 minutes)
Step 19. Hire an arborist to assess rotting tree limbs (1 day)
Step 20. Order a high-capacity dumpster for non-toxic debris (30 minutes)
Step 21. Rent a power washer from the local hardware store (1 hour)
Step 22. Deep clean the respirator masks for future use (45 minutes)
Step 23. Scrape flaky lead paint from the exterior shed walls (5 hours)
Step 24. Cut down dead branches hanging over the play area (3 hours)
Step 25. Call the city to report illegal dumping on the property line (20 minutes)
Step 26. Purchase specialized sealant for hazardous materials (45 minutes)
Step 27. Identify areas with invasive, skin-irritating plants (1 hour)
Step 28. Clear a path through the yard for safe equipment access (2 hours)
Step 29. Dig up and remove patches of poison ivy (4 hours)
Step 30. Sort metal scrap from organic waste (3 hours)
Step 31. Drain the stagnant, green pool water (6 hours)
Step 32. Uproot thorny bushes blocking the emergency exit (2 hours)
Step 33. Map out the location of broken glass shards (1 hour)
Step 34. Transport all collected hazards to the processing center (4 hours)
Step 35. Test the soil for heavy metal contamination (2 days)
Step 36. Buy industrial-grade gardening gloves and loppers (1 hour)
Step 37. Remove large fallen logs that harbor snakes (3 hours)
Step 38. Load the dumpster with heavy debris (5 hours)
Step 39. Clear out the rotted wood from the compost pile (2 hours)
Step 40. Buy specialized bins for sharp metal objects (1 hour)
Step 41. Print out the hazardous material manifest (10 minutes)
Step 42. Conduct a safety briefing for the cleanup crew (30 minutes)
Step 43. Excavate the area around the old septic tank (1 day)
Step 44. Secure the perimeter with "Do Not Enter" yellow tape (30 minutes)
Step 45. Document the removal process with photos for insurance (1 hour)
Step 46. Reserve a trailer for hauling away old tires (15 minutes)
Step 47. Cover the remediated ground with fresh, clean topsoil (5 hours)
Step 48. Disassemble the collapsed wooden deck (8 hours)
Step 49. Review the original property survey for hidden hazards (2 hours)
Step 50. Post a "Yard Safe" certificate on the gate (5 minutes)
